Every so often…I come across a product that just takes my skincare routine to a whole new level. Sometimes I see amazing results, sometimes really good results for an exceptionally good price, or it’s even just the texture/feel/experience of the product that makes it really special. The Living Cleansing Balm (also from Then I Met You) was one of the first products for me that fell into this category…The Giving Essence is another.  There are a lot of things about this essence that remind me of all the others I have tried in the past (especially those considered “first essences”). The Giving Essence has a very thin/watery consistency that absorbs nicely and layers well. You’ll find some fermented ingredients here along with brightening and hydrating ones too…again pretty much par for the course for a lot of essences. But, it’s what Then I Met You has done to heighten some of these benefits that makes it truly unique.  Right out of the box this essence really interested me. The glass bottle is painted in a similar fashion to the Birch Milk Refining Toner…but this time the paint kind of fades away/tapers off to reveal the bright pink hue of the essence itself. This really is some unique packaging that I don’t think I have seen before.   That pink color comes naturally from the Black Chokeberry Extract in the formula. In addition, there are just so many hydrating and antioxidant rich ingredients here (and in high concentrations) it would be hard to list them all. But some of the standouts include Galactomyces/Aspergillus/Saccharomyces Ferment Filtrates (the first three ingredients), Ellagic Acid (a powerful antioxidant and anti-aging ingredient), Red Algae Extract, Turmeric Root Extract, and Eggplant Extract (excellent for calming and soothing the skin).   In addition, Polyglumatic Acid is here…which might be the most interesting one on the list. Polyglumatic Acid has been trending in skincare for the past couple of years…but I don’t think I have used a product that featured it in a higher concentration (or at all that I remember). Basically, it is a humectant/peptide that holds 4-5 times more moisture compared to Hyaluronic Acid.   This highly concentrated and well-formulated essence made it’s intentions clear with the first application. Just a 5-6 drops of product and…how do I describe it…it’s like a total bomb of hydration and cooling! I honestly don’t know how Then I Met You pulled this off. Each time I use it I look into my palm like “How in the world does this little bit make my skin feel/look like I did a full 7 Skin Method?” It truly is IN-CRE-DI-BLE how hydrating The Giving Essence is. As a bonus, the Black Chokeberry provides a natural/tart scent that is very faintly cranberry-like…so refreshing. I found myself doing a total of two layers to include my face and neck.  All of the lovely fermented ingredients are also in full force providing some great brightening effects, not only right out of the gate…but over time as well. I really started to see these benefits take shape in this (my 4th) week with the product. Supported by a vitamin c serum as well as some chemical exfoliation (from the Birch Milk Refining Toner) many of the dark spots/areas of hyperpigmentation on my skin have improved. And generally, my skin has just looked more even-toned and “happy” I guess LOL!  Behind the scenes this essence uses a lot of antioxidants and skin supporting ingredients that don’t really provide a “wow” factor…but are just as great to have. I feel like my skin has become a bit more resilient in the face of chemical/physical exfoliation as well as having a better ability to hold onto moisture throughout the day. Once again, everything seems to just be…happy.  So clearly, I love this product! But just like the Birch Milk Refining Toner we have to talk about the cost. This essence comes in at $50.00 USD for 100ml. Although nowhere near as pricey as something like the SK-II Essence…The Giving Essence isn’t cheap. But because of the concentration of ingredients, the immediate AND long term benefits, and the need to only use a small amount per application I think this product is 100% worth every penny. Considering the formulation…I could absolutely see this essence being sold by a more “luxury” skincare brand for $75-100 USD. I’ve never used a high-end essence from brands like SK-II, Amore Pacific, or Tatcha. But to be honest…I don’t think I need to now.   I really poured over some of my reviews of favorite skincare products from the last year or so thinking about what I loved about them. For me…finding a product that combines effective ingredients, real/lasting results, and a unique experience usually means it is a winner. I have tried and loved quite a few in my day (LOL!)…but I have to say that The Giving Essence is in all honesty the best skincare product I have ever used.   For someone like me who struggles to keep skin hydrated to prevent excess oil/sebum production while also tackling hyperpigmentation it doesn’t really get any better than this essence. I could totally see myself moving away from hydrating toners and lightweight serums in favor of this one product. Cleanse, Exfoliate, The Giving Essence, Moisturize/SPF…done. Of course, I am a total skincare nerd with a closet full of stuff so that wont be happening anytime soon LOL!  Those with dry skin will also love this essence for the same reasons. That burst of hydration is something I haven’t experienced before and it really is long lasting.   I’m kind of glad that I got a chance to try a lot of other essence products before finding this one. I feel like without knowing the performance of products like the Missha Time Revolution First Treatment Essence, Secret Key Starting Treatment Essence, Neogen Real Ferment Micro Essence, and May Coop Raw Sauce (aka the ones I’ve liked LOL)…I wouldn’t be able to realize how The Giving Essence is all of those and more. When I do finally retire from the skincare reviewing world…I’ll be taking The Giving Essence with me.  There aren’t too many products I use that “call” me to my routine each morning and night but The Giving Essence is truly one of them and it is the highlight of my current skincare routine.  Bottom line, if you can…you should.

I was really impressed with this ampoule sample. I feel like I’ve tried just about every topical form of hyaluronic acid out there, and this ranks high on my lists of favorites for a few reasons. First of all, water-soluble sodium hyaluronate is my preferred form of HA because its molecules are small enough to actually penetrate skin and draw water inside the tissue, rather than just attract moisture temporarily to the surface. Additionally, I love the texture of this HA. It’s not so fluid that it feels like patting water on your face, but it’s not so gel-like that it begins to pill once you layer a moisturizer or oil on top. It has a wonderful tacky finish that I look for in my most-loved HA serums because it acts like a primer for whatever you use to seal it in. This also reminds me of the importance of sealing an HA - if left exposed to dry air, HA can actually have the exact opposite effect you want. HA is a humectant, meaning it draws water to itself - ideally from the air for the benefit of your skin. But HA isn’t self-aware, and if the atmosphere is drier than your skin and you haven’t sealed in your HA, the molecule is so good at its job that it can begin to pull moisture away from your skin, causing dehydration. So always protect your HA from greedy dry air! This ampoule is a great one to try if you’d like to experience the amazing results of this powerful ingredient.

It feels like just a few days ago when I was sitting in on a Zoom call hosted by Charlotte Cho...where she revealed/announced the Good Skin Days line.   I was so happy and excited for her and this next step in the Soko Glam journey. Needless to say, I picked up the three initial product launches as soon as I could and got my hands on the fourth (the Prime Time Cleansing Toner) last week.  But, I’ll save my thoughts on the new line as a whole for the full brand review. Right now I want to focus on one product (the first that I’ve incorporated into my routine)...the C’s The Day Serum.  When Charlotte first brought this serum up during her presentation I thought “Wait, you already have a vitamin c serum...and it’s one of my favorites!” The Cosrx Triple C Lightning Liquid was one of the very first K-Beauty products I purchased and it was the one that kind of sold me on vitamin c.  That product contained a powerful concentration of L-Ascorbic Acid that, for the first time, really started to fade my hyperpigmentation and acne scars. Issues I had been dealing with for literal decades finally started to show improvement and I was hooked. At that point, Soko Glam and Charlotte Cho could do no wrong in my eyes (I guess that is still the case LOL)!  Now that the Triple C Lightning Liquid has been discontinued (which hurts my heart but I understand given some of the stability and storing issues) we have this new serum to take its place...to a certain extent. Let’s dive in.  The C’s The Day Serum is a lightweight/fluid product featuring 10% Ascorbic Acid, Camu Camu Fruit Extract (for added vitamin c power), Licorice Root Extract, Niacinamide, Japanese Goldthread Extract, Ginseng Berry Extract, Hibiscus Flower Extract, and Cocoa Extract.  This blend of ingredients claims to not only provide the brightening/antioxidant boost of vitamin c but the other extracts heighten the antioxidant abilities even more. These ingredients can be great to fight against free radicals and block potential damage from sun exposure (not in a sunscreen protection manner however).  I love the clean/simplistic packaging and printed testimonials on the boxes. I’ll cover packaging and marketing in the brand review but let’s just say I’m left feeling impressed by Good Skin Days in an aesthetic and “purpose” perspective.  The actual serum comes out in a dropper format and applies/smoothes onto the skin really easily. It’s not quite as fluid as the Cosrx Lightening Liquid meaning you have a few seconds of “play” before the product drips off of the face. However, I found it to be easier to just apply a few drops to my hands...and then pat the product into my skin.  It had been quite some time since I had a vitamin c product in my routine...so I did experience some slight tingling on my skin. This was a bit more intense on areas that I shave (jawline and cheeks). But, after a few uses (I use this every AM) this effect totally went away and the C’s The Day Serum was just as comfortable as any other serum in my routine.  One of the things I really appreciated about this formula was the lack of tackiness or sticky feeling after application. This was something I had come to accept with concentrated vitamin c serums but this one was much more comfortable/approachable. I’ve never found it to be a real issue as I am usually applying several “steps” over my vitamin c...but those that dislike the feeling have little to worry about here.  After the first week or so of use I really noticed an improvement in overall skin brightness and tone-evening. Those that are hoping to find a direct replacement to that classic vitamin c serum from Cosrx...I really don’t think this is it. Don't get me wrong, I really like the C’s The Day Serum. But, it just doesn't have that super high concentration (and the volatility that comes with it) to really get in there and lighten the darkest of hyperpigmentation.   For me, the C’s The Day Serum is something that is more geared towards those just starting with vitamin c or who have previously experienced sensitivity to the ingredient. It does the job of moderate/overall brightening really well...but would point to the By Wishtrend Vitamin C 21.5% Advanced Serum as a more direct replacement for the Cosrx Triple C Lightning Liquid. That one is much more “intense” and suited for spot treatment use.  But, what is lost in regards to potency over the Cosrx product is made up for by how easy it is to “care” for this vitamin c. No refrigeration, no clogged pipettes, no off color (at least in the month that I’ve had mine open) are to be seen here. This is a really well formulated and stabilized vitamin c in my opinion that once again lends itself to a wider customer base (aka people like me that dont want the hassle).  I wouldn’t be providing a proper comparison without mentioning my all-time favorite vitamin c serum...the Glow Recipe Pineapple-C Bright Serum. That product uses a blend of Ascorbic Acid alongside Pineapple Fruit Extract and Lactic Acid to not only brighten the skin long-term...but also give an immediate “glow”. I love the versatility and instant results of that product so, so much.   The C’s The Day Serum offers similar results over time but is missing that instant “hit” of brightening and glow. But, coming in at nearly half the cost...it is a fine and affordable option that I think so many people are going to fall in love with (I certainly have)!  This is a total win from the Good Skin Days line and one that is worth picking up if you are in the market for a nice, easy to get along with, easy to care for, relatively affordable, and effective vitamin c serum. I ended up incorporating the Rovectin Skin Essentials Activating Treatment Lotion into my routine a few days after the Skin Essentials Conditioning Cleanser from the same line. I didn’t think there would be any issue with them clashing in my routine…but I wanted to give the cleanser a bit of time to do its thing (and check for any bad reactions) before adding the Treatment Lotion.  This is a product that can be used as a toner, essence, or even lightweight serum/ampoule depending on how you want to work it into your routine. The consistency of this product is quite thick…so some people may find it more comfortable to use later on than others. Personally, I started using this product as a toner…but ended up swapping it with the I’m From Mugwort Essence as that product is lighter and more comfortable to put on underneath (for me).  Featured ingredients here include 7 different forms of Hyaluronic Acid, Niacimamide, Caffeine, Panthenol, Licorice Root Extract, Chamomile Flower Extract, Centella Asiatica Extract, and Papaya Fruit Extract. This viscous toner/essence/whatever you want it to be (LOL) is free from alcohol, synthetic fragrance, and essential oils.   Right out of the gate I knew this product would be something unique. The slightly heavy/thick consistency is really interesting…shaking the bottle to catch air bubbles in the formula is kind of fun LOL! Just from the looks of it I was reminded of the Klairs Supple Preparation Toner. And the similarities don’t stop there (we’ll get to it).  Application is what you would expect…just a few drops of this product into the palm of the hand to be patted in. Then, continue to layer as you see fit. I ended up only being able to handle two layers of this super hydrating product before my skin was totally drenched. A little really does go a long way with this product.   With the seven forms of Hyaluronic Acid I expected this product to be thoroughly hydrating and hold on to moisture really well. And, it totally lived up to that expectation. After each use my skin was left feeling deeply hydrated…but the larger forms of Hyaluronic Acid that stayed closer to the surface seemed to hold onto hydration from serums. After a layer of moisturizer on top…my skin just felt so thoroughly hydrated and plump. Not a small feat while on Tretinoin.   In addition to the heavy dose of hydration…I was honestly shocked to see a reduction of redness/irritation as well as some mild brightening from this product. The addition on Caffeine, Niacinamide, and calming extracts really did work here and wasn’t a gimmick (in my opinion). True to their roots/mission…Rovectin seems to have created a product that delivers for people suffering from intense redness, dryness, and irritation.   One of the reasons I decided to work this product into my routine when I did was because I started Curology/Tretinoin not too lang afterwards. I wanted my skin to be in as hydrated/prepped of a state as possible. I think the Rovectin Skin Essentials Activating Treatment Lotion really helped to bring me there and keep my skin relatively happy considering all that I have been hitting it with LOL!  The only knock I have against this product is the slight sticky/tacky feeling that I noticed after application. Even though the Klairs Supple Preperation Toner only has one form of Hyaluronic Acid…the consistencies of the products are similar and I found Klairs’ offering to absorb and just feel nicer on the skin after application. It’s not a deal breaker (I found the stickiness to totally go away after applying serum/moisturizer)…but those trying to compare the two may want to take note.   I love the Rovectin Skin Essentials Activating treatment Lotion. It was such a key player in keeping my skin happy and hydrated over the last month or so. I prefer the finish of the Klairs Supple Preparation Toner…but I have to pick the Rovectin Lotion as the ultimate winner for its more robust/hydration focused formula and the addition of redness reducing ingredients. I’ve tried both the original and unscented versions of the Klairs SP Toner but still find Rovectin to be a step above.   Just like the Rovectin Conditioning Cleanser…I think all skin types will play well with this product. But, those who are battling frequent redness, irritation, or dryness will really be impressed with the abilities/results here. I’ll be keeping one of these on hand as I continue to use Curology…but I’m looking forward to switching to a more watery toner. I love my “7-skins method” and have missed layering and layering a nice/cooling toner.

Soko Glam was one of the very first e-retailers that I shopped when discovering K-Beauty in 2018. And since then it has pretty much become a staple for me when building my routine/stocking up on favorites.  And while Soko Glam has always kept a nice blend of mainstay (everyone knows them) brands and ones that are a little more under the radar...I feel like in the past year Soko Glam has really upped their “indie skincare brand” curation game.  To be honest, some of their offerings I wasn’t very versed on (Rovectin, Beauty of Joseon, and Re:p)...but I had at least seen them mentioned a couple of times here and there (EuniUnni on YouTube always finds the latest products!). But then, Solved Skincare appeared...and was the first brand curated to Soko Glam that I truly had 0% knowledge of.   From there, I stumbled upon Juice To Cleanse (reviews coming soon) as well as the brand/product I have been using recently...Inward Skincare. Specifically, their Agas ACue Herbal Mask.  Initially...I was a little hesitant to even read deeper into Inward. The rather long and hard to decipher name of their products (Agas ACue) left me a bit confused and Missha-fied lol! I didn’t really know what to make of them or how they might benefit my skin.   After “sleeping” on the products for a couple of months I finally decided to pull the trigger once I saw what the Agas ACue Herbal Mask actually looked like. The gel/wash-off style mask looked absolutely incredible. Being a fan of the I’m From Mugwort Mask...this product from Inward immediately drew my attention (which is a theme throughout this review).  The amazing looking gel consistency of the Agas ACue Herbal Mask is speckled with little green/leafy pieces while the gel itself has a decadent amber hue. One look on the Soko Glam page for this product/brand and I knew I wanted it on my face.  From there...things got better. The ingredients list for this product reads like a “traditional” K-Beauty (aka Hanbang) dream come true lol! Green Tea Leaf Powder, Glabrous Sarcandra Herb Extract (a medicinal herb used for soothing), Korean Dogwood Extract, and Japanese Nutmeg Extract from the island of Jeju (which is used for its anti-inflammatory properties and is quite rare) all seemed so appealing.   But, the star ingredient of this mask as well as all of the offerings from Inward (through Soko Glam) is Agastache Rugosa Extract...aka Korean Mint. This ingredient is one that I have not seen highlighted in other K-Beauty products (but is where the line gets its “Agas” moniker). However, it seems like such an ideal “hero ingredient” comparable to mugwort/artemisia in that it has similar calming and soothing effects. In addition, Korean Mint is listed as one of the 50 fundamental herbs in Chinese herbalism/”traditional medicine” for its antibacterial properties.  This wash-off mask...featuring all of its more traditional ingredients, is packaged in a clean/sleek/modern format. The idea of historied ingredients brought to the modern skincare world through formulation sat really deeply with me. It’s the same feeling I had when using the Acwell Traditional Grain/Syrup Sheet Masks back in 2018 (now much harder to come by unfortunately).  Application/use of the Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask was much more pleasant/approachable than what I was expecting. Where the I’m From Mugwort Mask can feel a little bit too thick/jelly-like...the Inward Herbal Mask has a much more thin and serum-like consistency that glides onto skin so much more easily.  The cooling and soothing effect of this mask was felt almost immediately for me while the real bits of green tea leaf helped to identify which parts of my face I had already coated in a nice layer. I found that I really “burned through” the I’m From Mugwort Mask because of the heavy application. My jar lasted about 6-8 applications before I ran out (which is a comment I have seen others make). The Inward Mask on the other hand goes on in thin/even layers...making it last a bit longer. I was able to get 9 uses out of it before writing this review...and I have enough for about 3 more.   Keeping this mask from Inward on for the recommended 5-10 minutes was an absolute dream for me (I honestly went a bit longer each time lol). The continued cooling effect was super relaxing and the scent...MY GOD the scent. Without any essential oils or synthetic fragrance, Inward has harnessed the natural scent of the concentrated ingredients to transport me to another place...  Imagine sitting on a bluff on the shores of Jeju. You’re relaxed...you’ve released the stress/worry of your normal life...just letting go and breathing in the mild aromas of the nearby Korean Mint field. Then, someone you love/adore approaches calmly...handing you a cup of green tea at the perfect temperature. You inhale...letting the warmth of the tea mingle with the fresh/minty breeze. That is what the Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask smells like.  “Inward...TAKE ME AWAY!”...a reference to the Calgon commercials of the 90’s that are probably really dating me lol!   Needless to say...the natural/herbal scent of this product had me hooked. And luckily, that experience totally overshadows what is a pretty messy rinse-off process. While the “gel” making up the majority of the Agas ACue Herbal Mask rinses relatively cleanly (in line with the I’m From Mugwort Mask)...the little bits of green tea can be a hassle to clean up. However, the “sticks/twigs” that are found in the I’m From product are much less prominent here and pose less of a risk for abrasion.  After all was washed away and I was left back in my bathroom (Hanbang dream-scape over lol)...I noticed a real improvement to my skin. Red blemishes had been calmed, my skin felt generally more smooth, and there was a reduction of excess oil/sebum that I really appreciated. The Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask seemed to provide what a hydrating/soothing mask would offer (like the I’m From Mugwort Mask) in addition to something more often seen by clay masks.  In the end...this mask ended up being the perfect mix of soothing, hydration, and clarifying that I have not seen before from a single product. To me, the Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask worked like the “advanced version” of the I’m From Mugwort Mask. Adding skin clarifying and pore clearing benefits with a texture/consistency that was much more approachable took the notion of gel-like herbal products to the next level.  I’m really working on avoiding claims like “GO BUY THIS” in my reviews...as I acknowledge that every person’s skin is different and has particular needs. But, I’m going to step away from that for a moment by saying…”If you have concerns about redness, oily skin, clogged pores, sensitive skin, breakouts...you need to give this one a look!”  The Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask is the product I have been waiting for...I see no reason why I won’t be able to replace both the I’m From Mugwort Mask and any clay mask I have been using with this single product. It's absolutely my new “must have” product that I look to when I am in need of both soothing and clarifying.  This wash off mask has been a dream and a delight to use over the past few weeks and is easily in the ranks for best product of the year (right alongside the Then I Met You The Giving Essence and Solved Skincare Coconut Oil Cleansing Pads).   I can’t wait to put together my “Best of 2020 List” where I am sure the Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask will make an appearance...and I look forward to hearing your thoughts on this product!

The cooling and soothing effect of this mask was felt almost immediately for me while the real bits of green tea leaf helped to identify which parts of my face I had already coated in a nice layer. I found that I really “burned through” the I’m From Mugwort Mask because of the heavy application. My jar lasted about 6-8 applications before I ran out (which is a comment I have seen others make). The Inward Mask on the other hand goes on in thin/even layers...making it last a bit longer. I was able to get 9 uses out of it before writing this review...and I have enough for about 3 more.   Keeping this mask from Inward on for the recommended 5-10 minutes was an absolute dream for me (I honestly went a bit longer each time lol). The continued cooling effect was super relaxing and the scent...MY GOD the scent. Without any essential oils or synthetic fragrance, Inward has harnessed the natural scent of the concentrated ingredients to transport me to another place...  Imagine sitting on a bluff on the shores of Jeju. You’re relaxed...you’ve released the stress/worry of your normal life...just letting go and breathing in the mild aromas of the nearby Korean Mint field. Then, someone you love/adore approaches calmly...handing you a cup of green tea at the perfect temperature. You inhale...letting the warmth of the tea mingle with the fresh/minty breeze. That is what the Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask smells like.  “Inward...TAKE ME AWAY!”...a reference to the Calgon commercials of the 90’s that are probably really dating me lol!   Needless to say...the natural/herbal scent of this product had me hooked. And luckily, that experience totally overshadows what is a pretty messy rinse-off process. While the “gel” making up the majority of the Agas ACue Herbal Mask rinses relatively cleanly (in line with the I’m From Mugwort Mask)...the little bits of green tea can be a hassle to clean up. However, the “sticks/twigs” that are found in the I’m From product are much less prominent here and pose less of a risk for abrasion.  After all was washed away and I was left back in my bathroom (Hanbang dream-scape over lol)...I noticed a real improvement to my skin. Red blemishes had been calmed, my skin felt generally more smooth, and there was a reduction of excess oil/sebum that I really appreciated. The Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask seemed to provide what a hydrating/soothing mask would offer (like the I’m From Mugwort Mask) in addition to something more often seen by clay masks.  In the end...this mask ended up being the perfect mix of soothing, hydration, and clarifying that I have not seen before from a single product. To me, the Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask worked like the “advanced version” of the I’m From Mugwort Mask. Adding skin clarifying and pore clearing benefits with a texture/consistency that was much more approachable took the notion of gel-like herbal products to the next level.  I’m really working on avoiding claims like “GO BUY THIS” in my reviews...as I acknowledge that every person’s skin is different and has particular needs. But, I’m going to step away from that for a moment by saying…”If you have concerns about redness, oily skin, clogged pores, sensitive skin, breakouts...you need to give this one a look!”  The Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask is the product I have been waiting for...I see no reason why I won’t be able to replace both the I’m From Mugwort Mask and any clay mask I have been using with this single product. It's absolutely my new “must have” product that I look to when I am in need of both soothing and clarifying.  This wash off mask has been a dream and a delight to use over the past few weeks and is easily in the ranks for best product of the year (right alongside the Then I Met You The Giving Essence and Solved Skincare Coconut Oil Cleansing Pads).   I can’t wait to put together my “Best of 2020 List” where I am sure the Inward Agas ACue Herbal Mask will make an appearance.

To be honest, I wasn’t really thinking I’d purchase this toner or the essence. When they came out I was full-on into my “must buy only natural/organic products that I can buy locally” phase. But, as I started to see some poor results from the products I was using I decided to come back to my K-Beauty roots LOL! This toner and essence duo from Then I Met You was my first purchase after making that decision.  This toner is a super lightweight/watery product that features Birch Juice, Marshmallow Root, Squalane, Glycolic Acid, and Lactic Acid. Shea Butter, Rose Flower Water, Olive Oil, and Wintergreen Leaf Extract all make it into the formula as well.  For those that are interested…this is a cruelty free product that is packaged in a soy printed box. The bottle itself is glass…but it is painted so I think recycling may be an issue here. For me, I love the aesthetic of this bottle/box so I’ll probably rinse it and hold on to it for some “vanity candy” LOL!   I have to say, I was pretty impressed with this product from the first use. Considering the Shea Butter, Olive Oil, and Squalane…I was really expecting a heavier product. This toner is just so thin and easily absorbed it kind of blew my mind. In my head I was thinking I would be left with a residue or heaviness like I did with the Laneige Cream Skin (review coming soon as well LOL) but this was totally different.  There is no added fragrance here or essential oils…so there really isn’t a “scent” exactly. But, the Glycolic and Lactic Acids come through for a slightly “acidic” scent I suppose. It reminded me a lot of some of the Dermalogica or Murad acid products I have used in the past. A very clinical/basic scent that I kind of like.  Even though there is Glycolic and Lactic Acid in the formula…the concentration is 1%. So, this is a product that can be used in place of your normal daily/hydrating toner. For me, I used it both AM and PM and applied 2 layers each time. Either applying this one to a cotton pad and swiping or just patting it in will work fine. Because “actives” like the ones used here are pH sensitive…I gave this product just a couple of minutes alone before moving onto my essence. There is some debate on how essential a “wait time” is for things like AHA/BHA/Vitamin C for them to be effective (or maybe more accurately how long that wait time should be). Personally its a habit to wait at this point so I tend to do it naturally.  Over the past month with the Birch Milk Refining Toner and I have to say I am a fan! My skin has been looking more hydrated/dewy and remaining that way longer into the day. I have totally cut out hydrating mists (for now) but my skin doesn’t seem to be thirsty for that extra hydration throughout the day. I think Then I Met You has performed some kind of magic by incorporating heavier emollients into such an incredibly light/watery toner.  However, there are a couple of things that keep me from making this a “must have” pick.   The low level of AHA here is totally fine for daily maintenance and super mild exfoliation…but cant really be relied on as the only means of exfoliation (at least for me). I decided to remove any other AHA products from my routine to see what this toner could do. And, it wasn’t much LOL! My blemishes/mild breakouts weren’t phased by this toner and I did see a bit of increased congestion around my cheeks and nose. My combination/oily/sebum-filled skin does need something a bit more intense from time to time (unfortunately). Or, I can get by with incorporating several “low-acid” products into my routine at once…so maybe a BHA cleanser, AHA toner, and a mild AHA/BHA wash-off mask. Alone, the Birch Milk Refining Toner just didn’t have what it takes.   For those with more normal skin or who are mildly dry/flaky…this could be a much better option for exfoliation. Especially if other products with higher percentages of AHA have been too intense for you. This isn’t a bad/ineffective acid toner…it was just a little too mild for me to totally rely on it. As a compliment to a weekly AHA/BHA mask or something like that…perfection LOL!  Aaaaand…we have to talk about the price. It is another reason I don’t think I could make this a consistent purchase. This product comes in at $32.00 USD for 100ml. Compared to some of my other favorite acid toners from Peach & Lily and Moon Juice…its actually the least expensive option. But, because I didn’t see the exfoliating benefit I see in those other products I’d rather pay a bit more. As for the hydration aspect, there are just sooo many other excellent hydrating toners for far less. My favorite from last year was the Aromatica Rosemary Refresh Toner (now the Vitalizing Rosemary Decoction Toner) can be found for around the same price…but you get 300ml.   I love Then I Met You…its philosophy, brand story, and founder Charlotte Cho are simply amazing. She is kind of the reason I decided to start writing reviews and sharing my thoughts on K-Beauty. I will continue to try their products at least once LOL but I don’t think I will be coming back to this toner.   However, if you have struggled to find an acid toner that is gentle enough for your skin this is a must try. Also, if you have used the Laneige Cream Skin or other toners that include oil/emollient ingredients and found them to be way too heavy or greasy…this might be your new holy grail!

The ACSEN Oil Cut Cleansing is intended as a first cleansing step before water based cleansing. What makes the product super unique/interesting is that it it not an “oil cleanser” in the traditional sense but rather a watery gel that is applied to the skin, massaged, and rinsed off. There is no real emulsification in the traditional sense here either…but the product claims to remove oil based products in a similar/equally effective way.  This product uses a variety of surfactants/emulsifiers that aid in breaking down oil/makeup/impurities on the skin. PEG-7 Glyceryl Cocoate, PEG-8, and Olive Oil PEG-7 Esters are all here…and are pretty common ingredients in cleansing/micellar waters. Outside of that…the rest of the ingredients list is pretty simple. Tree Moss Extract, Korean Pepper Extract, Korean Pasque Flower Extract, Aloe Leaf Juice, and Papaya Fruit Water are also in the formulation. Finally, synthetic fragrance comes last on the list.  As I mentioned above…the texture or “vehicle” for these emulsifying ingredients is unique in that it is a gel as compared to an oil. The product applies similarly to a watery serum and needs to be massaged/moved around fairly quickly to avoid dripping. There is a clean/fresh/floral scent to this product that isn’t overwhelming and totally disappears after rinsing. Fragrance is still one of the things that turns me off to the Troiareuke ACSEN product’s but I don’t mind it as much with this product (and even then it isn’t the fragrance as a concept that I dislike…I just don’t really love the actual scents of the products).  Massaging and rinsing off this product is pretty straightforward and similar to what you would expect from a typical cleansing oil. The ACSEN Oil Cut Cleansing glides over skin nicely and never feels like it is pulling or dragging at the skin. However, some of the product seemed like it absorbed into my skin after about 30 seconds…so I felt the need to generously apply this product to get the “slip” I desired through the entire 1-3 minutes of massaging.   The Troiareuke ACSEN Oil Cut Cleansing rinses very easily and thoroughly without residue left behind. This is a major plus for those with combination/oily skin that dislike traditional cleansing oils for this reason. In addition, I’ve felt as though my skin is left looking/feeling hydrated more so than I expected. This product seemed to help carry hydration through my second cleansing step and into toning if that makes sense LOL!  Overall, I was really happy with this product over first couple weeks of use. It seemed to do a fine job of removing excess oil, sebum, and non-waterproof sunscreen fine enough. My water based cleanser may have needed to pick up the slack a bit more than it normally would…but not drastically so. It wasn’t until I switched to a waterproof sunscreen in the last week that things changed for the worse.  With several layers of heavy/waterproof sunscreen on…the ACSEN Oil Cut Cleansing just didn’t have what it takes 100% to break everything down. It took a bit more massaging, and a bit more product than I would normally use (which was already quite a bit in my opinion) to thoroughly cleanse my skin. I’m not a makeup wearer…but I assume similar issues would arise with long-wear/waterproof makeup.   All that being said…I think this is a great option for specific skin types/uses. If you have oily skin that doesn’t play well with oil cleansers, and don’t use heavier sunscreens/makeup…this is a must try. But, anyone outside of that may find this product to be lacking. For me, it felt/acted like a basic micellar water…just dressed up in a gel form and priced higher than I would like. It’s not something that I would personally come back to (I have no problem with more traditional oil cleansers) but I might recommend it in certain circumstances.   Not really a ringing endorsement I know LOL.

Once I got things in order (LOL) I found the cleansing foam to perform beautifully. I have used a few pump style water based cleansers in my skincare “journey”…but this one from Solved Skincare is one the best. Combination/oily skin types will love the balance between thorough cleansing and not stripping the skin of natural oils while those with dry skin will appreciate the hydrated/refreshed feel after use. The omission of essential oils and fragrance means that this product should be approachable for those with sensitive skin/damaged skin barrier. A win in my book and one that I will come back to in the future.

Although it is super convenient to have both day and night creams in one jar, easy for travel, the results of the cream were extremely underwhelming. Both the day and night creams are very lightweight and absorb into your skin within minutes (even though the day cream looks and feels much thicker than the night). They both have pleasant, light scents - the night being more dominated by lavender and the day more of a refreshing smell. All that being said, after using the both creams daily for over a month now, I can honestly say that my skin has gotten worse. My pores and fine lines are way more visible, and my skin texture looks uneven and rough. I have to say that I won't be buying this again. I purchased this in the 7 day mask challenge set that you can buy here on the SoKo website. This mask was a weird one for me, because I actually have never really been a mask type of person, and I didn't know that there are three layers to the mask. There are two cotton-y and rigid layers that hold together an almost jelly-like mask on the inside.   You only have to take off one of the cotton-y layers to get to the jelly-like one. This is the layer that actually sticks to your face and it does a pretty good job of it. I did not know this when I put on the mask initially and it was not sticking to my face!!! The real spots that I noticed it worked were on my forehead. I am only 27, but I have some wrinkles in spots of my forehead because I show my emotions on my face. When I was finished using this mask, the spot between my eyebrows was not wrinkling at all, even after purposefully doing so, and the fine line on my forehead was severely diminished. I have yet to see how this hold up throughout the week, but for the day that I used this on, it really made a difference.   My only gripe is on how thick this is, but maybe it is a good thing for my dry skin. My face was still tacky after using it, and I had to opt for not applying any product because it would probably be too much product for the whole day. If any of you think that is a plus, then I think maybe this is the product for you. I think I am just not used to this because I usually have to put on a few more products to keep my skin hydrated the whole day. I had debated on putting my sunscreen to go outside for the day, and decided I should do it, but it was too much on face face for the day.   I suggest this for nighttime, for that reason, as it's too heavy with other products. Will I repurchase this? Probably. I go through packs of patches and microdart patches a month just because I have severe cystic and regular acne. I use ~15 microdart patches a month and it gets expensive very quickly. Acropass is the most affordable (but effective) one I've tried. Make sure to stock up during sales!   Microdart patches work best when the acne is in its beginning stages. You know that feeling when you feel a pimple coming up. Depending on the stage/size of the acne, it may not get rid of it right away, but it improves the healing process. A large cystic acne that would take at least a month to reduce in size heals within a week for me. Do not use this on surface acne (like white heads). You want a regular hydrocolloid patch for that.   For this product, the active ingredients are in the cleansing pad. Don't just swipe it once onto the skin. I would rub it over the area like a toner. Then peel, stick, and press onto the patch for a few seconds to make sure the dart penetrates the skin. And leave it on overnight ideally. If not, leave it on for at least 2 hours. I don't put a patch on the same spot the next day. Instead I put a regular pimple patch over it the next day and will put another microdart patch again a few days later if I feel I need it. I found using a microdart patch (from any brand) on the same spot every day made my acne get more irritated and take longer to heal.
